newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees oil stocks drawdown in Jan/March.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees oil stocks drawdown in Jan/March.

text.p: World stocks of oils and fats will fall to 9.70 million tonnes by April 1, from 11.08 million at the start of 1997, independent newsletter Oil World said in its latest report, issued earlier this week.
It said the quarterly stocks decline would compare with a 0.44 million tonne fall in the same 1996 quarter and a 10-year average of 0.36 million tonnes for the quarter.
First demand would develop quickly in China, India and Indonesia, while production would fall in Latin America, China, the EU-15 and the former USSR.
This would cause large shifts from stocks in exporting countries in Southeast Asia, the U.S. and South America to stocks in importing countries.
Global soyoil stocks were pegged at 2.69 million tonnes at the start of the year, falling to 2.35 million by April 1, seven percent lower than a year earlier.
The figures applied to 15 seed oils and animal fats but excluded olive oil and butter.
